slices.name: Deal intake, triage draft, and the pipeline board
slices.objective: As a relationship manager I submit a borrower's loan request with its documents on the Deal Intake screen, and the deal is created at the intake stage with its exposure and approval tier derived deterministically; the intake triage agent then drafts a classification, a missing-document list, and a proposed analyst queue as a PENDING draft that no one can bypass, and every active deal with its current stage appears on the Pipeline Board. Canonical stage slugs used by the whole app, in order: intake, document_extraction, financial_spreading, risk_grading, memo_drafting, policy_compliance, tiered_approval, closing. Exposure = the requested facility amount alone; approval_tier is derived from it: <= $250,000 = analyst, $250,000-$1,000,000 = officer, > $1,000,000 = committee. Deals are addressed by their client-supplied deal_reference. Seeded role accounts identify actors: rm.rivera (relationship manager), an.chen (credit analyst), co.brennan (credit officer); HTTP callers name the actor with an explicit acting_user / submitted_by field in the body while the UI uses the signed-in identity, and every create and transition writes an append-only audit row.
